rows.title: Senior Customer Insights Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Welcome to KFC. Home of the real ones.We sell the world’s best chicken. Seriously. And we’ve done it since 1939, when the idea of crispy, original recipe chicken took Kentucky by storm. Now, we’re proud to serve 1000+ communities across the UK and Ireland, bringing the grit, pride and iconic reputation that we started with, all those years ago.
Across the Restaurant Support Centre (RSC), we come to work to be ourselves, and to make something of ourselves. We want to see our potential go that little bit further, as part of one of the world’s most iconic brands.
What’s the gig? Well, you support our restaurants - and we’ll support you every step of the way. Simple. Our doors are open - and they can take you anywhere.
All we ask is that you be you. Because that makes us, us. Sound good? Great. Let’s find out about that job.
THE TEAMOur Tech team is a 60+ strong team of curious minds, building the digital experiences that power KFC – from app to kiosk, delivery to checkout. We work cross-functionally, move fast, and stay focused on what matters: creating smart solutions that make things better for our customers and our teams.
ABOUT THE ROLEAt KFC, we have millions of customers choosing us every week, across restaurants, drive-thrus, kiosks, delivery and digital. That creates a lot of data. The exciting bit is what we do with it.We’re looking for a Data Analyst, Loyalty & CRM to help us better understand our customers, how they behave and what keeps them coming back for more.
Sitting within our Data & Analytics team and partnering closely with Loyalty, CRM and Marketing, you’ll dig into customer, transactional and marketing data to uncover insights that can genuinely influence what we do next.
You might be exploring why certain customers visit more frequently, identifying opportunities to increase loyalty and retention, understanding which campaigns actually changed behaviour, or spotting a commercial opportunity hidden within millions of transactions.
Yes, you’ll build brilliant reporting. But this role goes much further than telling us what happened. We want someone curious enough to ask why it happened, why it matters and what we should do about it.
If you love solving problems with data, understand customers and can turn complex analysis into a story that gets people to act, this could be for you.
WHAT YOU’LL SPEND YOUR TIME DOING
Customer Analytics & Insight
You’ll help us understand our customers better and turn that understanding into commercial opportunities.You’ll:Analyse customer, transactional, loyalty and marketing data to identify trends, behaviours, risks and opportunities.Measure how our Loyalty programme is performing and identify opportunities to improve engagement, retention and customer value.Build customer segmentation and behavioural analysis to support more relevant, personalised experiences.Understand customer acquisition, frequency, spend, retention and lifetime value.Evaluate campaigns, promotions and loyalty activity to understand what’s working and where we can improve.Turn complex datasets into simple, actionable recommendations.Proactively look for opportunities where insight can improve customer experience and commercial performance.
Reporting & Visualisation
Great decisions need data people can trust and understand.You’ll:Build, automate and maintain dashboards using Power BI and other reporting tools.Create clear reporting across customer behaviour, loyalty, campaign effectiveness and commercial performance.Establish consistent KPIs and reporting standards across Loyalty and Marketing analytics.Make sure reporting is accurate, scalable and easy to understand, whether the audience is technical or not.Continuously improve how we work through better automation, data quality and simpler reporting.
Business Partnering
This isn’t an analyst role where you disappear into the data and send someone a spreadsheet.You’ll:Partner closely with Loyalty, CRM and Marketing to understand the business problem before jumping into the analysis.Act as the dedicated Data & Analytics partner for Loyalty, helping turn questions and opportunities into clear analytical approaches.Work across Commercial Finance, Digital, Operations, Technology and the wider Data & Analytics team.Partner with Data Engineering to make sure the data you need is available, trusted and fit for purpose.Present insights and recommendations to stakeholders across the business.Help us build a culture where data and evidence genuinely influence the decisions we make.
WHAT WE’D LOVE FROM YOUWe’re looking for someone who combines strong analytical capability with real commercial curiosity.
You’ll ideally bring:Strong SQL skills and confidence interrogating large datasets independently.Experience with Power BI or similar reporting and visualisation tools.Experience working with customer, transactional or commercial data.Exposure to cloud data platforms such as Snowflake.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a great eye for detail.An understanding of data quality, validation and governance.Strong Excel capability.Experience delivering analytics within Customer, Marketing, CRM, Loyalty or another commercially focused environment.Examples of using data and insight to influence a commercial or strategic decision.Confidence working cross-functionally and explaining analysis to people who don’t live and breathe data.
A degree in a relevant discipline is useful, but equivalent professional experience is just as valuable.Even better if you have...CRM, loyalty or customer engagement analytics experience.Customer segmentation or behavioural analytics experience.Experience measuring marketing and campaign effectiveness.GA4 or other digital analytics experience.Knowledge of customer lifetime value, attribution or incrementality.Experience with experimentation, A/B testing or statistical analysis.Exposure to platforms such as Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud or Adobe Campaign.
 ABOUT YOUYou’re naturally curious. Finding the answer is great, but you’ll probably have another three questions once you get there.You’re commercially minded and want your analysis to lead somewhere, whether that’s a better customer experience, smarter campaign or stronger commercial result.You can take something complicated and make it simple.You’re comfortable challenging assumptions and following the data rather than looking for the answer someone wants to hear.You enjoy partnering with different teams and building relationships, rather than working in a silo.You’re proactive, organised and comfortable juggling priorities in a fast-moving environment.You’re always looking for a smarter, simpler way of doing things.And, of course... a true KFC believer.
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU:We offer benefits that make your life that little bit easier, because we know the juggle is real.From flexible, hybrid working to Fri-Yay early finishes and Live Well Days, we’ve created a package that supports the real you, in and out of work.
You’ll get:Hybrid working from our Woking RSC (just 24 mins from London). The tech team come into the office 2 days per week.Up to 11% company pension contributionsFri-Yay finishes at 1pm every Friday25 days’ holiday (plus bank hols) a5 Live Well Days a year, just for youBonus scheme linked to company & personal performancePrivate healthcare, Digital GP access & mental health coachingEnhanced parental leave and flexible return optionsStudy support, income protection, life cover & moreAnd yes—25% off the chicken
Because real ones deserve real rewards.
THE ROAD TO BECOMING A REAL ONE...Apply (Go on... do it) – send us your CV and answer a couple of app questions.Intro call with our Talent TeamVirtual call with Hiring Manager + another team memberVirtual call with Stakeholers F2F interview & Task at our HQ, Home of The Real Ones in Woking
KFC FOR EVERYONE:Whoever you are and wherever you’re from, KFC is a place where you can bring the real you to work.
Our promise is this: every person who applies to a role at KFC, regardless of age, background, ethnicity, gender, ability, religion or sexual orientation, will have an equal opportunity to work here. We don’t just welcome, we encourage applications from underrepresented groups from all industries.
If you’d like any additional support with your application, have a disability or condition that may affect your performance during the recruitment process, or have any other requirements - just let us know. We’ll be there to help you be the real you.
Ready?We hope so, if you’re ready to be part of our community, now’s the time to apply.
Worried you aren’t ticking all the boxes? Don’t - we’d still love to hear from you.
Beware of fake job postings using Yum! and/or our brand logos -- KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and Habit Burger & Grill -- on fraudulent sites. Yum! Brands only posts jobs on official careers pages and never asks for money during onboarding. Avoid unsolicited contacts via Telegram, WhatsApp or similar social apps.

rows.title: Emerging Content Creator Programme
rows.descriptionText:
Emerging Content Creator Programme
We’re looking for 4–5 ambitious emerging creators to join Magari’s first Emerging Content Creator Programme.
The three-month programme is designed to help emerging creators develop their personal brand, content and audience, while working with us to build Magari’s own platform and community.
As part of the programme, you’ll get access to our £1,000 Creator Content Fund to help bring new projects and ideas to life, alongside guaranteed and performance-based financial rewards. You’ll work with us to create original content, grow Magari’s audience and community, and help shape the brand from an early stage.
You don’t need to be an established influencer with hundreds of thousands of followers. We’re looking for people who already take creating seriously and have the ideas, ambition and potential to grow.
About Magari
Magari is on a mission to redefine luxury for the digital age.
We’re building a new kind of membership, bringing together premium products, services, expertise and experiences in a connected ecosystem designed around the lives and interests of our members.
We believe modern luxury is about more than labels. It’s about discovering exceptional products, trusted recommendations and experiences that genuinely add value to our lives.
At the heart of Magari will be a growing community of brands, creators, experts and partners helping us shape what the next generation of luxury retail looks like. Creators joining this first programme will come on board at an early stage and have the opportunity to play a meaningful role in shaping what we build.
Launching soon in the UK.
What you’ll get
£1,000 Creator Content Fund — access to a shared fund designed to help our creators develop more ambitious content and build their personal brand. The fund can support selected projects through videography, photography or editing; products and experiences; locations; creator collaborations; and paid amplification.
Guaranteed payment + performance upside — receive a £120 participation fee over the three-month programme, alongside the opportunity to earn up to £795 in performance fees, with additional bonuses for exceptional contribution and results. Selected content may also be separately commissioned and paid.
Individual support — regular one-to-one sessions to discuss your goals, develop ideas, plan projects and work through the practical challenges of growing your creator platform.
A creator network — join a small cohort of ambitious emerging creators, collaborate on content and introduce your work to new audiences.
What we’ll create together
Over the three-month programme, we’ll aim to develop around 3–5 pieces of content with each creator.
We’ll develop ideas together that work for your own platform as well as Magari. The programme is designed to give creators the resources to experiment and pursue more ambitious ideas, without compromising their individual voice or creative direction. Projects might include creator collaborations, experiences, interviews, reviews or longer-form content, with selected projects supported by the Creator Content Fund.
The programme is designed to fit alongside your existing work and creator activity, rather than requiring a fixed weekly time commitment.
We’ll also ask creators to help introduce Magari to new audiences and prospective members, participate in the wider Creator Collective and share honest feedback as we develop the brand.
Who we’re looking for
You don’t need a huge following to apply. What matters is that you take creating seriously and have a genuine ambition to grow your creator business.
You might create around beauty, fashion, food, wellness, fitness, travel, culture, career, motherhood or London life — or something we haven’t thought of yet. We’re particularly interested in people with a distinctive point of view, interesting stories and passions of their own, whose interests and ambitions extend beyond social media.
You should:
Be based in the UK.Already be creating content consistently and demonstrate a genuine commitment to it.Have interests, ideas and a perspective that extend beyond sponsored content.Be open to collaboration, experimentation and feedback.
There is no minimum follower requirement. We expect many applicants to have around 3,000–10,000 followers or subscribers, but quality, commitment and potential matter more to us than current audience size.
London and the South East are preferred, although we welcome applications from creators elsewhere in the UK who are happy to spend some time in London.
Instagram will be important, but we’re also interested in people creating across YouTube, TikTok and Substack.
Programme details
Duration: 3 monthsPlaces: 4–5 creatorsContent: Around 3–5 collaborative pieces over the programmeCreator Content Fund: £1,000 shared across the cohortGuaranteed participation fee: £120 per creatorPerformance fees: Up to £795 per creatorLocation: UK; London and South East preferred
How to apply
Apply through LinkedIn Easy Apply by 31 October.
Before applying, please make sure your LinkedIn profile includes links to the social or content channels where you create, so we can get a sense of your work.
Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we’ll contact applicants we’d like to speak to directly through LinkedIn.
You can also follow the Magari LinkedIn page to keep up with the programme and what we’re building ahead of launch.

rows.title: Applied AI Engineer, Beneficial Deployments (Life Sciences - Clinical Trials/Drug Repurposing)
rows.descriptionText:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Beneficial Deployments

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences - focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

About The Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team. This is a partner-facing role: you'll support nonprofits, research institutes, academic medical centres and public-sector funders as they use Claude to get treatments to patients with rare and neglected diseases, where there is little or no commercial incentive to fund development.

The role focuses on two areas where we think Claude can help these partners today. The first is clinical trials. Trials in these diseases have small patient populations, investigator-led or nonprofit funding and little operational support, and they often stall on protocol quality, operational risk and site start-up. Claude can help teams design better trials and start them sooner. The second is drug repurposing: finding new uses for approved, usually off-patent or generic medicines, whose known safety profiles can let a good hypothesis reach patients years sooner than a new molecule.

You'll advise and embed in partners' teams, building alongside their engineers, scientists and clinicians.

Responsibilities

Work with partners' trial teams to design, review and prioritise clinical trials with Claude: drafting and reviewing protocols and statistical analysis plans, and flagging enrolment and operational risks.Build and validate tools that help partners find new uses for approved, mostly off-patent medicines in rare and neglected diseases, from literature, omics and patient data, and assemble the evidence so the partner can decide the next step.Build reusable infrastructure other institutions can adopt (MCP servers for biomedical data sources, agent skills, benchmarks grounded in real clinical questions), and feed what you learn in the field back to product, engineering and research.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have

Hands-on experience designing, running or analysing clinical trials, or finding new uses for existing medicines. Deep experience in one; both are a bonus. Having contributed to a regulatory submission for a trial is a plus.Comfort with biomedical data: literature, omics, and real-world patient data (health records, registries, claims), ideally inside secure or trusted research environments.Strong engineering skills: you can take an LLM-powered tool from prototype to production code, and write evals to measure it.Experience working directly with external partners or customers in a technical role.Clear written and verbal communication: docs other institutes can use without you, and results clinicians trust.A scrappy mentality: you're comfortable in ambiguity, wear several hats, and do what it takes to get a result for a partner.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

£225,000—£255,000 GBP

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

rows.title: Campus Recruiting Analyst/Associate
rows.descriptionText:
About Millennium

Millennium is a global, diversified alternative investment firm, founded in 1989. Defined by evolution, innovation and focus, Millennium’s mission is to deliver results for our investors.

Our people are empowered with both independence and support: the autonomy to pursue ideas with conviction and the backing of a global network committed to collaboration, disciplined risk management and continuous learning. With opportunities to deepen expertise and accelerate development, talent at Millennium is equipped to adapt, evolve and build lasting impact over time. Discover how transformative growth accelerates impact.

Meet the Team

The Human Resources Department covers the full spectrum of HR disciplines. Through high-touch, impactful solutions, the team helps optimize organizational performance and fosters a workplace and culture that attracts, engages, and retains exceptional talent. EMEA Campus Recruiting is a key area of focus within the broader HR team, supporting the firm’s continued growth across the region.

What You'll Do

 Support the full recruitment lifecycle for undergraduate and graduate candidates, from sourcing and interviewing through offer management and onboarding. Partner with hiring managers and stakeholders to define hiring needs, build robust talent pipelines, and develop effective campus recruiting strategies. Develop and execute innovative university recruitment strategies across EMEA, including London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, Paris, and Switzerland. Partner closely with hiring managers throughout the recruitment process and summer internship programs. Plan and deliver on-campus and in-house recruiting events that strengthen Millennium’s university presence and candidate engagement. Build strong relationships with candidates and new hires, ensuring a seamless, high-quality experience throughout the recruiting process. Support the planning and management of the internship program across multiple phases of the candidate and intern lifecycle. Maintain clear, proactive communication with stakeholders and candidates while identifying challenges and proposing practical solutions.

What You Bring

 Strong understanding of the campus recruiting lifecycle and university hiring processes. Prior Campus or university recruiting experience; financial services experience is a plus. Ability to build trusted, collaborative partnerships with senior stakeholders and hiring managers. Demonstrated ability to anticipate challenges, develop innovative ideas, and drive effective solutions in a fast-paced environment. Strong talent attraction and candidate engagement capabilities. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Experience using an applicant tracking system to manage candidate pipelines and recruiting activity.

All we ask is that you be you. Because that makes us, us. Sound good? Great. Let’s find out about that job.
THE TEAMOur Tech team is a 60+ strong team of curious minds, building the digital experiences that power KFC – from app to kiosk, delivery to checkout. We work cross-functionally, move fast, and stay focused on what matters: creating smart solutions that make things better for our customers and our teams.
ABOUT THE ROLEAt KFC, we have millions of customers choosing us every week, across restaurants, drive-thrus, kiosks, delivery and digital. That creates a lot of data. The exciting bit is what we do with it.We’re looking for a Data Analyst, Loyalty & CRM to help us better understand our customers, how they behave and what keeps them coming back for more.
Sitting within our Data & Analytics team and partnering closely with Loyalty, CRM and Marketing, you’ll dig into customer, transactional and marketing data to uncover insights that can genuinely influence what we do next.
You might be exploring why certain customers visit more frequently, identifying opportunities to increase loyalty and retention, understanding which campaigns actually changed behaviour, or spotting a commercial opportunity hidden within millions of transactions.
Yes, you’ll build brilliant reporting. But this role goes much further than telling us what happened. We want someone curious enough to ask why it happened, why it matters and what we should do about it.
If you love solving problems with data, understand customers and can turn complex analysis into a story that gets people to act, this could be for you.
WHAT YOU’LL SPEND YOUR TIME DOING
Customer Analytics & Insight
You’ll help us understand our customers better and turn that understanding into commercial opportunities.You’ll:Analyse customer, transactional, loyalty and marketing data to identify trends, behaviours, risks and opportunities.Measure how our Loyalty programme is performing and identify opportunities to improve engagement, retention and customer value.Build customer segmentation and behavioural analysis to support more relevant, personalised experiences.Understand customer acquisition, frequency, spend, retention and lifetime value.Evaluate campaigns, promotions and loyalty activity to understand what’s working and where we can improve.Turn complex datasets into simple, actionable recommendations.Proactively look for opportunities where insight can improve customer experience and commercial performance.
Reporting & Visualisation
Great decisions need data people can trust and understand.You’ll:Build, automate and maintain dashboards using Power BI and other reporting tools.Create clear reporting across customer behaviour, loyalty, campaign effectiveness and commercial performance.Establish consistent KPIs and reporting standards across Loyalty and Marketing analytics.Make sure reporting is accurate, scalable and easy to understand, whether the audience is technical or not.Continuously improve how we work through better automation, data quality and simpler reporting.
Business Partnering
This isn’t an analyst role where you disappear into the data and send someone a spreadsheet.You’ll:Partner closely with Loyalty, CRM and Marketing to understand the business problem before jumping into the analysis.Act as the dedicated Data & Analytics partner for Loyalty, helping turn questions and opportunities into clear analytical approaches.Work across Commercial Finance, Digital, Operations, Technology and the wider Data & Analytics team.Partner with Data Engineering to make sure the data you need is available, trusted and fit for purpose.Present insights and recommendations to stakeholders across the business.Help us build a culture where data and evidence genuinely influence the decisions we make.
WHAT WE’D LOVE FROM YOUWe’re looking for someone who combines strong analytical capability with real commercial curiosity.
You’ll ideally bring:Strong SQL skills and confidence interrogating large datasets independently.Experience with Power BI or similar reporting and visualisation tools.Experience working with customer, transactional or commercial data.Exposure to cloud data platforms such as Snowflake.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a great eye for detail.An understanding of data quality, validation and governance.Strong Excel capability.Experience delivering analytics within Customer, Marketing, CRM, Loyalty or another commercially focused environment.Examples of using data and insight to influence a commercial or strategic decision.Confidence working cross-functionally and explaining analysis to people who don’t live and breathe data.
A degree in a relevant discipline is useful, but equivalent professional experience is just as valuable.Even better if you have...CRM, loyalty or customer engagement analytics experience.Customer segmentation or behavioural analytics experience.Experience measuring marketing and campaign effectiveness.GA4 or other digital analytics experience.Knowledge of customer lifetime value, attribution or incrementality.Experience with experimentation, A/B testing or statistical analysis.Exposure to platforms such as Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud or Adobe Campaign.
 ABOUT YOUYou’re naturally curious. Finding the answer is great, but you’ll probably have another three questions once you get there.You’re commercially minded and want your analysis to lead somewhere, whether that’s a better customer experience, smarter campaign or stronger commercial result.You can take something complicated and make it simple.You’re comfortable challenging assumptions and following the data rather than looking for the answer someone wants to hear.You enjoy partnering with different teams and building relationships, rather than working in a silo.You’re proactive, organised and comfortable juggling priorities in a fast-moving environment.You’re always looking for a smarter, simpler way of doing things.And, of course... a true KFC believer.
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU:We offer benefits that make your life that little bit easier, because we know the juggle is real.From flexible, hybrid working to Fri-Yay early finishes and Live Well Days, we’ve created a package that supports the real you, in and out of work.
You’ll get:Hybrid working from our Woking RSC (just 24 mins from London). The tech team come into the office 2 days per week.Up to 11% company pension contributionsFri-Yay finishes at 1pm every Friday25 days’ holiday (plus bank hols) a5 Live Well Days a year, just for youBonus scheme linked to company & personal performancePrivate healthcare, Digital GP access & mental health coachingEnhanced parental leave and flexible return optionsStudy support, income protection, life cover & moreAnd yes—25% off the chicken
Because real ones deserve real rewards.
THE ROAD TO BECOMING A REAL ONE...Apply (Go on... do it) – send us your CV and answer a couple of app questions.Intro call with our Talent TeamVirtual call with Hiring Manager + another team memberVirtual call with Stakeholers F2F interview & Task at our HQ, Home of The Real Ones in Woking
KFC FOR EVERYONE:Whoever you are and wherever you’re from, KFC is a place where you can bring the real you to work.
Our promise is this: every person who applies to a role at KFC, regardless of age, background, ethnicity, gender, ability, religion or sexual orientation, will have an equal opportunity to work here. We don’t just welcome, we encourage applications from underrepresented groups from all industries.
If you’d like any additional support with your application, have a disability or condition that may affect your performance during the recruitment process, or have any other requirements - just let us know. We’ll be there to help you be the real you.
Ready?We hope so, if you’re ready to be part of our community, now’s the time to apply.
Worried you aren’t ticking all the boxes? Don’t - we’d still love to hear from you.
Beware of fake job postings using Yum! and/or our brand logos -- KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and Habit Burger & Grill -- on fraudulent sites. Yum! Brands only posts jobs on official careers pages and never asks for money during onboarding. Avoid unsolicited contacts via Telegram, WhatsApp or similar social apps.

rows.title: Senior Marketing Manager
rows.descriptionText:
A little bit about usAirmic’s Purpose is to champion the societal and strategic value of risk management and insurance in a changing world. We are the UK and Ireland's largest risk management and insurance association with over 400 corporate and around 2,000 individual members, supported by a network of leading risk, insurance, legal, technology and consulting partners, and affiliated institutes, associations, universities and business schools. Our members enjoy access to a wide variety of face to face and online events and learning opportunities, special interest groups and regional meetings, supported by a competency framework and mentoring scheme. With over 400 CPD hours, networking opportunities, and a growing research library, Airmic supports professionals at all career stages in navigating and shaping the future of risk management.
Airmic is mid-way through a significant digital transformation. Three changes make this role pivotal:
A new platform. Airmic is moving from a fragmented Microsoft Dynamics and DotDigital stack to ReadyMembership, an integrated membership platform delivered by Pixl8, going live at end of March 2027. It brings CRM, events, payments, email and website into one system.A consolidated website and email estate. Microsites are being retired into a single site with six pillars (Membership, Events, Learning, Thought Leadership, Partners, About and News).A refreshed brand and marketing strategy. A new brand architecture and a July 2026 to June 2027 marketing strategy built on three pillars: Engage, Retain, Acquire.
The platforms and plans are in place. Airmic now needs someone who can turn them into consistently excellent campaigns, and who will own ReadyMembership as a marketing platform long after the implementation team steps away.
About the roleThe Senior Marketing Manager will own Airmic's campaign plan and marketing platform: setting campaign objectives, building the audience and automation infrastructure in ReadyMembership, and being accountable for the engagement, retention and acquisition results that follow.
The Head of Membership and Marketing sets direction and owns the annual strategy. The Senior Marketing Manager turns that strategy into a costed campaign plan with numeric targets, delivers it across Airmic's channels, and reports on results. The role also contributes to developing the marketing plan itself, bringing campaign performance data and member and partner insight to shape priorities, targets and budget. Colleagues in Events, Learning, Research and Commercial use the role as their route into marketing.The role is hands-on where it matters most: the successful candidate will personally design segments, lifecycle journeys, templates and landing pages in ReadyMembership. It also runs Airmic's core channels directly (social media, email and newsletters, paid media and web content), using agencies and freelancers for design and specialist work.
Key Responsibilities1. Campaign planning and commercial accountability (around 25%)Manage the Engage, Retain, Acquire strategy into a 12-month campaign plan in Monday.com, with a numeric objective, audience and budget for every campaign.Input into and contribute to developing Airmic's annual marketing plan with the Head of Membership and Marketing, using performance data and audience insight to recommend priorities, targets and budget allocation.Enable the outcomes of Airmic's revenue campaigns: corporate and partner membership acquisition and renewal, Annual Conference delegate, partner and exhibitor sales, and learning programmes such as Risk Management Fundamentals and NextGeneration.Hold the campaign budget, including agency and freelance spend, and report return on investment.Write campaign briefs that set objectives, key messages and channel mix, then deliver or commission the channel activity that follows.Approve campaigns and sends within delegated guardrails, escalating strategic or reputational messaging to the Head of Membership and Marketing.
2. ReadyMembership and marketing automation ownership (around 30%)Act as the business owner of ReadyMembership's marketing functions: Email Centre, segmentation, automated journeys, event promotion, web content and landing pages.Join the implementation team from early 2027 as a key user, shaping configuration, testing campaign workflows and signing off marketing readiness before go-live.Design and build the lifecycle journeys: new member onboarding, renewal, lapsed re-engagement, event nurture and non-opener re-engagement.Design the segmentation model and own the email category taxonomy and send governance: suppression, consent (Legitimate Interest basis), frequency caps and deliverability.Set and enforce email standards, including single-subject, single-call-to-action discipline and approved templates.Set marketing data quality standards (contact records, segment definitions, tagging) and work with membership operations to maintain them.Provide first-line platform support and training for marketing use, escalating to Pixl8 where needed.
3. Channel marketing delivery (around 20%)Manage and grow Airmic's LinkedIn and wider social presence, with a content plan tied to the campaign calendar.Plan, build and send campaign emails and newsletters, moving from DotDigital to ReadyMembership's Email Centre at go-live.Plan and run paid media with a specialist 3rd party media agency (LinkedIn Ads, Google Ads) against campaign objectives and budget.Write and commission content for web, email and social, and produce simple visual assets from approved brand templates, briefing designers for anything larger.Keep marketing-led website pages current across the six site pillars.
4. Member and partner insight, and measurement (around 15%)Define the marketing measurement framework and own the dashboard: engagement, conversion, renewal, event registration and revenue attribution by campaign.Engage actively with external stakeholders, members and partners (through SIGs, events, member forums and partner meetings) to build insights that help develop campaigns, propositions and messaging.Work with partner and sponsor marketing teams on joint campaigns, representing Airmic's audience and marketing standards.Commission and use member and delegate research, such as conference feedback surveys, to test and refine campaign propositions.Design testing programmes across lifecycle and campaign activity, and turn results into changes to the plan.Report monthly to the Head of Membership and Marketing, and prepare marketing input for leadership and board reporting.
5. Internal marketing partnership and governance (around 10%)Run the marketing intake and prioritisation process for Events, Learning, Research and Commercial, with agreed turnaround times and a clear route for "no" or "not yet".Chair a monthly campaign planning meeting that aligns the campaign plan with content, channel and SIG calendars.Own campaign brand governance under the new brand architecture: "Airmic [Product]" naming, approved templates, and the Tier 1 treatment of the Annual Conference.Build marketing capability across Airmic through guidance, templates and training, so colleagues can self-serve routine activity in ReadyMembership.Select and manage agency and freelance partners.Represent marketing in cross-organisational planning forums, and deputise for the Head of Membership and Marketing when required.
The roleThis position is full time, 35 hours a week from Monday to Friday. The job holder will operate from the Airmic office in Marlow House, Lloyd’s Avenue, City of London. There is a requirement to work three days per week (minimum) in the Airmic office with the balance of the time working from home. Tuesday is currently a team “core” day in the office where we come together and organise a team lunch. There will be occasional travel within the UK, such as to venues for Airmic events, including the 3-day Airmic Annual Conference and Exhibition to be held in Liverpool in July 2027. It's a great and fun way to meet our partners and members!
About youThe ideal candidate would have the below expertise and experience however if you don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. Research shows that some candidates — particularly women — are less likely to apply unless they meet nearly 100% of the criteria, while others may apply when meeting far fewer. If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you!
The ideal candidate has helped shape a marketing plan, owned a budget and a marketing automation platform, engages confidently with senior external stakeholders, and can show commercial results in numbers.
Essential AttributesSeven or more years in marketing, including at least three owning campaign plans and their outcomes at manager level or above.Accountability for a marketing budget and for commercial targets such as new business, renewal or event revenue.Experience contributing to the development of an organisational marketing plan or strategy, not only delivering one.A track record of engaging directly with external stakeholders (members, customers, partners or sponsors) and turning that insight into campaign propositions and messaging.Confident representing the organisation with senior external stakeholders.Hands-on ownership of a CRM or marketing automation platform (for example ReadyMembership, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, HubSpot or Dynamics Customer Insights), including designing segmentation models and automated lifecycle journeys, not only sending campaigns.Business-side experience of a platform migration or new system launch: requirements, testing, data preparation and adoption.Recent hands-on channel experience across LinkedIn, email and paid media (LinkedIn Ads, Google Ads), with results to show.Has built a measurement framework or dashboard and used it to change a plan or reallocate budget.Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR and PECR for B2B email, including Legitimate Interest and suppression management.Proven ability to influence heads of department and prioritise competing demands without direct authority.Strong editorial judgement: able to brief, edit and sign off copy for a senior professional audience.
Desirable AttributesMembership body, professional association or B2B events experience, particularly subscription renewal and conference sales campaigns.Familiarity with financial services, insurance or risk management audiences.Experience working with an implementation partner or SaaS supplier through a rollout.Line management or coaching experience.CIM Diploma or equivalent professional qualification.

rows.title: Talent Partner (Financial Services) - AI Scale-up
rows.descriptionText:
Talent Partner (Financial Services)Compensation: up to £100,000 + bonus + equityLocation: London, on-site
Hawkwood is partnering with one of the fastest-growing enterprise AI companies in financial services as it continues to build its London and European organisation.
The company has raised more than $300m, with a reported valuation of approximately $2bn. It is backed by some of the world's leading tech investors, including Sequoia and Thrive Capital, alongside strategic investment from a number of major global banks.
Having established significant traction in the US, the business is now investing heavily in its international expansion. As part of that growth, they are looking for an experienced recruiter to take ownership of hiring across their strategic financial services organisation in London and Europe.
This is a unique recruiting challenge. You'll build relationships with high-calibre front-office professionals across investment banking, private equity, hedge funds, trading and corporate finance, engaging people who may not have previously considered leaving traditional finance for a technology company.
You'll work closely with the company's Co-Founder, senior business leaders and EMEA Talent leadership to define the profiles they need, map the market and build long-term pipelines of finance talent. The role combines the rigour and relationship-building of executive search with the pace, ownership and breadth of an in-house role at a rapidly scaling AI company.
The company operates with a high-performance, high-ownership culture, so this is an opportunity for someone who wants to build networks, solve difficult talent problems and play a key role in shaping how an international organisation scales.
What you'll do:
Build and own proactive pipelines of high-calibre front-office finance talent across London and Europe, spanning investment banking, private equity, hedge funds, trading, corporate finance and adjacent investment backgrounds.Lead full-cycle recruitment, from market mapping and initial engagement through screening, interview management, offer negotiation and close.Partner closely with the cofounder and senior business leaders to define roles, calibrate talent profiles and establish what exceptional finance talent looks like as the European organisation grows.Develop long-term relationships with passive candidates, creating talent communities and networks rather than relying primarily on active applicants or transactional sourcing.Help position the company as a compelling career destination within London and European finance, engaging relevant alumni communities, referral networks and industry events.Build talent segmentation and market-mapping frameworks that give leadership a clear view of the strongest talent pools across different financial institutions, functions and European markets.Act as a trusted advisor on the external talent market, bringing insight around candidate availability, compensation, competitors and the realities of persuading high-performing finance professionals to move into AI.Operate comfortably across both strategy and execution, from challenging and refining a hiring brief to personally sourcing, engaging and closing candidates.Use recruiting technology, data and AI tools to identify pipeline gaps, improve workflows and build a more scalable approach to hiring as the organisation grows.Deliver a high-quality candidate experience throughout, recognising that many of the people you engage will be making a significant and potentially unconventional career move.
You will bring:
5+ years of recruiting experience, ideally with meaningful exposure to front-office financial services, investment professionals or another highly competitive talent market.A strong understanding of the London financial-services talent landscape, with European market exposure particularly valuable.Excellent proactive sourcing and market-mapping capability, with a track record of identifying and engaging high-performing candidates who are not actively looking to move.The credibility and communication skills to engage bankers and investors who are progressing successfully within prestigious and highly compensated traditional career paths.Strong relationship-building instincts and an interest in developing genuine networks and talent communities rather than relying on high-volume outbound activity.Commercial judgement and the confidence to advise senior stakeholders on talent strategy, challenge assumptions and help shape a brief rather than simply execute against it.The ability to operate with both search-level rigour and startup pace, managing multiple concurrent searches without compromising the quality of talent or candidate experience.High agency and genuine comfort with ambiguity. You'll be joining an international organisation that is still being built, so priorities will evolve and there won't always be an established process to follow.Intellectual curiosity around finance, AI and technology, and an ability to articulate why someone with a successful career in traditional finance might choose to apply their experience to transforming the industry instead.
We recognise how challenging this current job market is for candidates, and Hawkwood are therefore striving to provide the best candidate experience we can. If you are interested in this opportunity, we kindly request that you apply via this LinkedIn advert, as opposed to sending us an email or LinkedIn direct message.

rows.title: Business Development Executive (Onboarding)

rows.title: Payment Operations Analyst

We believe that businesses of all sizes deserve better financial and payment products and services. Traditionally, businesses of all sizes are let down by slow applications, protracted onboarding, opaque pricing, restrictive contracts and forced to use outdated solutions that no longer meet the innovative requirements of modern business.

We started our journey four years ago, and have since helped tens of thousands of Australian businesses reduce the complexity and time taken to take and make payments, manage complex fleets of payment hardware, store and save money and lead the conversation in business-to-business fintech. We’re now taking our next steps in expanding our industry and world leading capabilities into the United Kingdom.

Our company is backed by leading global VCs, and brings together experienced payment and tech industry professionals who are aiming to redefine business banking and the way businesses get paid by their customers.

If you are passionate, curious, hungry and seeking an opportunity to make your mark on Fintech in the United Kingdom, with the strength of a global team behind you - we’d love to talk to you. This is a unique opportunity to shape, direct and build better financial services for all UK businesses.

Zeller is searching for a Payment Operations Analyst to join our team. Reporting to the Payment Operations and Treasury Lead, you'll play an instrumental role in shaping and growing Zeller's payment operations.

This is a hands-on, strategic position where you'll be a key part of ensuring our payment processes are seamless and secure. You'll investigate disputes and transaction issues, becoming the go-to expert for providing clear and timely responses to customers, vendors, and internal teams. Your work will be crucial in ensuring compliance with financial regulations and building trust with our merchants.

This role is ideal for a detail-oriented problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced environment. Your strong analytical skills and ability to communicate complex information will be key to your success. We’re excited to meet someone ready to make an immediate impact on a rapidly growing fintech, helping us build a robust and reliable financial platform for businesses across the UK.

Responsibilities

Disputes ManagementMonitor and manage the dispute process for various payment rails including Mastercard, Visa, FPS, BACs whilst ensuring compliance and high customer satisfaction. Promptly escalate and take ownership of issues affecting payment operations, collaborating with internal and external teams for resolution.Reporting & GovernanceEnsure daily and monthly reconciliation of internal accounts is accurate and timely. Perform payment rails reporting in compliance with regulatory obligations. Continuously recommend and enhance procedures, document processes, and refine SLAs. Assist in developing business requirements for product enhancements.Stakeholder & Merchant RelationsServe as the primary contact and escalation point for payment scheme inquiries and business-as-usual projects. Coordinate with merchants for debt recovery.


Experience And Skills

Minimum 2 years of experience in payment operationsUnderstanding of UK safeguarding rulesProficiency in card dispute resolution, as well as BACSs and FPS dispute processes.Experience in implementing process improvements and handling escalation proceduresChallenges the status quo, working autonomously and collaboratively.Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.Highly organised, disciplined, and detail-obsessed.Proven reliability in data processing, problem-solving, and meeting deadlines.


Bonus points

Experience in high-growth environments, Financial Services, or EMI/Payments.Proficiency in SQL and BI tools.


Like the rest of the team, you’ll benefit from

 An opportunity to shape and build the future of Zeller from the ground up in the UK A competitive salary package, including equity from an early stage; A balanced, progressive, and supportive work environment; Endless learning and development opportunities;Excellent parental leave and other leave entitlements;Being part of a fast-growing and ambitious scale-up.


At Zeller, we celebrate diverse perspectives and experiences, and strongly encourage people of all backgrounds and identities to apply to join our team.

rows.title: Data scientist
rows.descriptionText:
At Bending Spoons, we’re striving to build one of the all-time great companies. A company that serves a huge number of customers. A company where team members grow to their full potential. A company that functions at unparalleled levels of effectiveness and efficiency. A company that creates value for shareowners at an extraordinary rate. And a company that does so while adhering to high ethical standards.

In pursuit of this objective, we acquire and improve digital businesses, not to sell on, but to own and operate for the long term. The transformations we make are often deep—designed to speed up innovation, benefit customers, and strengthen business performance. Here, hierarchy is minimal and teams are small and talent-dense. We operate established products with the ambition, agility, and urgency of a startup. Across the company, we integrate AI deeply into how we work so that human judgment and machine intelligence reinforce each other.

For a talented, driven, and collaborative individual, working at Bending Spoons is an opportunity to learn, make an impact, and progress their career at an exceptionally high rate. That’s our promise to such a candidate.

A few examples of your responsibilitiesDesign and improve data pipelines. Contribute to the design and evolution of data systems—ensuring data is accurate, reliable, and efficiently processed across diverse tech stacks.Ensure data correctness and scalability. Work closely with software engineers to validate data, define metrics, and improve the robustness of reporting and analytics systems.Develop internal data products and tooling. Help build scalable solutions (e.g., reporting engines, forecasting tools) used by product teams across the company.Support platform-wide decision-making. Partner with multiple teams to provide the analytical and modeling backbone for business planning and performance tracking.Leverage AI to accelerate work and uncover insights. Use AI tools to move faster, surface ideas and opportunities, and study competing products and trends.

What we look forReasoning ability. Given the necessary knowledge, you can solve complex problems. You think from first principles, and structure your ideas sharply. You resist the influence of biases. You identify and take care of the details that matter.Drive. You’re extremely ambitious in everything you do—and your initiative, effort, and tenacity match the intensity of your ambition. You feel deeply responsible for your work. You hold yourself to a high—and rising—bar.Team spirit. You give generously and without the expectation of receiving in return. You support the best idea, not your idea. You're always happy to get your hands dirty to help your team. You’re reliable, honest, and transparent.Proficiency in English. You read, write, and speak proficiently in English.

What we offerIncredibly talented, entrepreneurial teams. You’ll work in small, result-oriented, autonomous teams alongside some of the brightest people in your field.An exceptional opportunity for growth. We go to great lengths to hire individuals of outstanding potential—then, our priority is to put them in the ideal position to thrive. Spooners in their 20s lead products worth hundreds of millions of dollars. And if you’ve got what it takes, you’ll soon be playing an essential role in major projects, too.All. These. Benefits. Flexible hours, remote working, unlimited backing for learning and training, top-of-the-market health insurance, a rich relocation package, generous parental support, and a yearly retreat to a stunning location. We help each Spooner set up the conditions to do their best work.Competitive pay and access to company equity at a discount. Typical annual salary offers range from £85,797 to £151,436 in London and from €66,065 to €107,837 elsewhere in Europe. The lower end of these ranges applies to candidates with little or no relevant experience, while exceptionally experienced candidates may receive offers of up to £316,052 in London or €240,330 elsewhere in Europe. Candidates offered a permanent contract may choose to receive part of their compensation in discounted company equity.

Commitment & contract
Permanent or fixed-term. Full-time or part-time.

Location
Milan (Italy), London (UK), Madrid (Spain), Warsaw (Poland), or fully remote from eligible countries.

The selection process
In our screening process, we prioritize verifiable signals of excellence, regardless of seniority. There are no preferential paths beyond what your application demonstrates, and we evaluate every candidate through the same process.

Some people hold back because they feel they lack experience or have an “imperfect” CV. If you like the role and believe you could excel over time, don’t self-reject.

All applications go through our careers page, which is the only way to be considered. If you pass our screening, you’ll be asked to complete one or more tests. They are challenging, may involve unfamiliar problems, and can take several hours. To learn more about what to expect throughout the selection process, you can find additional information here.

We set the bar high and won’t extend an offer until we’re confident we’ve found the right candidate. This is why a job may remain open for months or be reposted several times.

We consider all applicants for employment and provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities—please let us know through this form.

Before you apply
If you’ve applied before but didn't receive an offer, we recommend waiting at least one year before applying again.

Bending Spoons is a demanding environment. We’re extremely ambitious and we hold ourselves—and one another—to a high standard. While this tends to lead to extraordinary learning, achievement, and career growth, it also requires significant commitment.

To help you ramp up quickly and set yourself up for success, we expect you to spend most days in our Milan office during your first few months with us, regardless of your long-term work location. It’s the best way to rapidly absorb our company culture and build trust with your new teammates. We’ll support you with generous travel and accommodation assistance. After that, you’re welcome to work from one of our offices, or remotely from approved countries—depending on what we agree at the offer stage.

If the role speaks to you and you’re excited to give your best, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now—we can’t wait to meet you.

rows.title: Applied AI Engineer, Beneficial Deployments (Life Sciences - Clinical Trials/Drug Repurposing)
rows.descriptionText:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Beneficial Deployments

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences - focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

About The Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team. This is a partner-facing role: you'll support nonprofits, research institutes, academic medical centres and public-sector funders as they use Claude to get treatments to patients with rare and neglected diseases, where there is little or no commercial incentive to fund development.

The role focuses on two areas where we think Claude can help these partners today. The first is clinical trials. Trials in these diseases have small patient populations, investigator-led or nonprofit funding and little operational support, and they often stall on protocol quality, operational risk and site start-up. Claude can help teams design better trials and start them sooner. The second is drug repurposing: finding new uses for approved, usually off-patent or generic medicines, whose known safety profiles can let a good hypothesis reach patients years sooner than a new molecule.

You'll advise and embed in partners' teams, building alongside their engineers, scientists and clinicians.

Responsibilities

Work with partners' trial teams to design, review and prioritise clinical trials with Claude: drafting and reviewing protocols and statistical analysis plans, and flagging enrolment and operational risks.Build and validate tools that help partners find new uses for approved, mostly off-patent medicines in rare and neglected diseases, from literature, omics and patient data, and assemble the evidence so the partner can decide the next step.Build reusable infrastructure other institutions can adopt (MCP servers for biomedical data sources, agent skills, benchmarks grounded in real clinical questions), and feed what you learn in the field back to product, engineering and research.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have

Hands-on experience designing, running or analysing clinical trials, or finding new uses for existing medicines. Deep experience in one; both are a bonus. Having contributed to a regulatory submission for a trial is a plus.Comfort with biomedical data: literature, omics, and real-world patient data (health records, registries, claims), ideally inside secure or trusted research environments.Strong engineering skills: you can take an LLM-powered tool from prototype to production code, and write evals to measure it.Experience working directly with external partners or customers in a technical role.Clear written and verbal communication: docs other institutes can use without you, and results clinicians trust.A scrappy mentality: you're comfortable in ambiguity, wear several hats, and do what it takes to get a result for a partner.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

£225,000—£255,000 GBP

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

rows.title: Associate Data Scientist
rows.descriptionText:
Department: Data & AILocation: UK - London

Description

Insurance isn’t the first industry most data scientists think of when they imagine cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) work, but the incredibly rich data and nature of the business make it a great place to put AI to use.

CFC's Data & AI team is building production agentic systems that automate complex underwriting decisions — not demos, not proofs of concept sitting on a shelf, but Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents and machine learning (ML) pipelines that drive real business outcomes. This role will sit alongside senior data scientists, machine learning engineers, and software engineers, as an analytical counterpart: running experiments, stress-testing assumptions, and generating the evidence that shapes what gets built and how to improve it over time.

This is an Associate Data Scientist role designed for someone early in their career who wants genuine exposure to production AI systems from day one. You'll work closely with, and have the opportunity to learn from, team members while contributing analysis and experimentation work that feeds into live services — such as statistical analysis and LLM evaluation. This will require the kind of careful, evidence-based thinking that makes the difference between an AI system that works in a notebook and one that holds up under real conditions.

The problems are genuinely hard. The data is complex, the decisions are high-stakes, and the domain has the kind of depth that keeps the work interesting. If you want to grow quickly in applied AI and ML — working on real systems, not toy datasets — this is the right environment.

About the role

Design and run experiments that directly shape production AI agents — testing ideas, validating approaches, and turning research into deployed improvements.Actively explore cutting-edge developments in AI and machine learning — with the space and support to experiment, prototype, and bring new techniques into production where they add value.Evaluate and refine LLM-powered workflows — building robust evaluation frameworks, stress-testing agent behaviour, and driving continuous quality improvements in live systems.Explore complex, real-world datasets to uncover insights that meaningfully improve underwriting decisions and system performance at scale.Prototype and iterate on features for AI/ML pipelines, taking ideas from early exploration through to measurable impact in production services.Investigate how agentic systems behave in production — identifying opportunities for improvement, failure modes, and ways to make systems more robust and reliable.Collaborate closely with ML/AI engineers to bridge research and production — contributing code, debugging issues, and shipping improvements end-to-end.Document and present experiments, findings, and methodologies clearly to both technical and business users, making sure insights are reproducible and decisions are traceable.

About you

You will have experience/be familiar with the following:

AI and LLMsFamiliarity with LLM-powered apps and services, evaluation frameworks, prompt engineering, and other generative AI work — whether through professional experience, coursework, or personal projects.Curiosity about how LLM-based systems behave in production and how to evaluate them rigorously.Experience with ML models (including deep models) and their lifecycle, including training, evaluation and inference.Exposure to experiment tracking tools (e.g. MLflow).Technical skillsProficiency in Python.Working knowledge of SQL for querying and preparing data.Comfort with Git and version control as part of a collaborative workflow.Basic grounding in CI/CD concepts and an interest in how software is tested and deployed.
Analytical foundationsSolid grounding in statistics and probability — comfortable with hypothesis testing, distributions, and drawing defensible conclusions from data.Hands-on experience with exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, and building and evaluating ML models.Working knowledge of the core ML model lifecycle: data preparation, training, validation, and monitoring.Working styleDetail-oriented and methodical — you care about getting the analysis right, not just getting it done.Clear communicator, able to summarise findings and explain analytical decisions to engineers and non-technical stakeholders alike.Comfortable asking questions and working under the guidance of senior engineers while progressively taking on more ownership.Intellectually curious — the kind of person who pulls on threads and wants to understand why, not just what.Nice to haveExposure to designing, implementing, and managing business-critical applications in a production environment.Working knowledge of how ML/LLM systems get productionized: CI/CD pipelines, release processes, monitoring/observability.Knowledge of the insurance domain (not expected — the domain complexity is part of what makes this interesting).

Core Values

Love what you do:
We show up each day ready to take on the world. Our passion and intensity set us apart and makes the difference to our colleagues, customers, brokers and carriers.

Challenge everything:
We’re never afraid to question the way that things are done and we constantly challenge ourselves and others to makes things better.

Have fun, be good:
Insurance is a serious business, but we don’t take ourselves too seriously. We make it fun to work at CFC, we welcome all viewpoints, and we treat everyone how we would expect to be treated.

Job Title

Job Description Summary

Job Description

rows.title: Associate Data Scientist
rows.descriptionText:
Department: Data & AILocation: UK - London

Description

Insurance isn’t the first industry most data scientists think of when they imagine cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) work, but the incredibly rich data and nature of the business make it a great place to put AI to use.

CFC's Data & AI team is building production agentic systems that automate complex underwriting decisions — not demos, not proofs of concept sitting on a shelf, but Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents and machine learning (ML) pipelines that drive real business outcomes. This role will sit alongside senior data scientists, machine learning engineers, and software engineers, as an analytical counterpart: running experiments, stress-testing assumptions, and generating the evidence that shapes what gets built and how to improve it over time.

This is an Associate Data Scientist role designed for someone early in their career who wants genuine exposure to production AI systems from day one. You'll work closely with, and have the opportunity to learn from, team members while contributing analysis and experimentation work that feeds into live services — such as statistical analysis and LLM evaluation. This will require the kind of careful, evidence-based thinking that makes the difference between an AI system that works in a notebook and one that holds up under real conditions.

The problems are genuinely hard. The data is complex, the decisions are high-stakes, and the domain has the kind of depth that keeps the work interesting. If you want to grow quickly in applied AI and ML — working on real systems, not toy datasets — this is the right environment.

About the role

Design and run experiments that directly shape production AI agents — testing ideas, validating approaches, and turning research into deployed improvements.Actively explore cutting-edge developments in AI and machine learning — with the space and support to experiment, prototype, and bring new techniques into production where they add value.Evaluate and refine LLM-powered workflows — building robust evaluation frameworks, stress-testing agent behaviour, and driving continuous quality improvements in live systems.Explore complex, real-world datasets to uncover insights that meaningfully improve underwriting decisions and system performance at scale.Prototype and iterate on features for AI/ML pipelines, taking ideas from early exploration through to measurable impact in production services.Investigate how agentic systems behave in production — identifying opportunities for improvement, failure modes, and ways to make systems more robust and reliable.Collaborate closely with ML/AI engineers to bridge research and production — contributing code, debugging issues, and shipping improvements end-to-end.Document and present experiments, findings, and methodologies clearly to both technical and business users, making sure insights are reproducible and decisions are traceable.

About you

You will have experience/be familiar with the following:

AI and LLMsFamiliarity with LLM-powered apps and services, evaluation frameworks, prompt engineering, and other generative AI work — whether through professional experience, coursework, or personal projects.Curiosity about how LLM-based systems behave in production and how to evaluate them rigorously.Experience with ML models (including deep models) and their lifecycle, including training, evaluation and inference.Exposure to experiment tracking tools (e.g. MLflow).Technical skillsProficiency in Python.Working knowledge of SQL for querying and preparing data.Comfort with Git and version control as part of a collaborative workflow.Basic grounding in CI/CD concepts and an interest in how software is tested and deployed.
Analytical foundationsSolid grounding in statistics and probability — comfortable with hypothesis testing, distributions, and drawing defensible conclusions from data.Hands-on experience with exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, and building and evaluating ML models.Working knowledge of the core ML model lifecycle: data preparation, training, validation, and monitoring.Working styleDetail-oriented and methodical — you care about getting the analysis right, not just getting it done.Clear communicator, able to summarise findings and explain analytical decisions to engineers and non-technical stakeholders alike.Comfortable asking questions and working under the guidance of senior engineers while progressively taking on more ownership.Intellectually curious — the kind of person who pulls on threads and wants to understand why, not just what.Nice to haveExposure to designing, implementing, and managing business-critical applications in a production environment.Working knowledge of how ML/LLM systems get productionized: CI/CD pipelines, release processes, monitoring/observability.Knowledge of the insurance domain (not expected — the domain complexity is part of what makes this interesting).

Core Values

Love what you do:
We show up each day ready to take on the world. Our passion and intensity set us apart and makes the difference to our colleagues, customers, brokers and carriers.

Challenge everything:
We’re never afraid to question the way that things are done and we constantly challenge ourselves and others to makes things better.

Have fun, be good:
Insurance is a serious business, but we don’t take ourselves too seriously. We make it fun to work at CFC, we welcome all viewpoints, and we treat everyone how we would expect to be treated.
